conversationalSummary.text: TODAY is probably one to skip—there’s just no reliable window, and the wind looks like the main let-down for Meio da Baia. Even with a rising push that can give a bit of shape at some point, Surfline is reading poor and the gusts could make it messy rather than rideable. I’d check Surfline and MEO Beachcam before you commit, and unless the cams look surprisingly better than expected, save the drive.

best.explanation: Meio da Baia looks like a solid window for Worth checking, Low confidence: 0.9-1.4 m, 140 kJ, 8 s period, consistent 76/100, and wind is the main risk.  An inconsistent Baía spot that can work well when north-northwest swell reaches the bay; this is best for bodyboard sessions when the bay is clean, there is enough period and size, and the forecast shows a defined wave; 6-9s at mid tide can make exposed beaches like Belgas / Almagreira / Cerro / Meio da Baia sharp and rippable.  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot; gusts over 35 km/h could make it messy.
best.shortExplanation: Meio da Baia is worth a quick check for after work (16:30 start), but it is not a guaranteed session.  Treat it as a check-first call rather than a sure thing.  Wind is the main thing to watch.  The tide and timing are lining up well for this spot.

ranked.explanation: Baleal looks like a fun-sized window for Too soft, Low confidence: 0.6-0.9 m, 65 kJ, 9 s period, workable consistency 58/100, and wind is the main risk.  A broad, forgiving beach setup with several peaks; this is best for spreading out and finding a manageable wave when the bay has enough push; worth keeping on the radar because Surfline is showing it above Poor while most other local spots are Poor..  Watch: wind angle is poor for this spot; 6-9s at mid tide is soft and sectiony on the Baleal sandbanks; Baleal looks below your bodyboard fun size; Baleal may feel too soft without more push.
